title: Optical Overlay Metrology - Micro-cracks Detection on Surfscan SP5
subtitle: Incoming Wafer QC Quality Validation for 3nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Amir Patel

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Surfscan SP5 system to detect and classify Micro-cracks defects during incoming wafer qc inspection at the 3nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 12 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Micro-cracks defects that are critical to yield at the 3nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Surfscan SP5 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Surfscan SP5
- Inspection Type: Optical Overlay Metrology
- Target Defect: Micro-cracks
- Process Step: Incoming Wafer QC
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 3nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 12

This test case applies to all Surfscan SP5 systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 12 for incoming wafer qc monitoring in the 3nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Surfscan SP5
Software Version: v11.5.331
Recipe: OPTICAL_OVERLAY_METROLOGY_3nm_INCOMING WAFER QC
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: High (111 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.5μm
Edge Exclusion: 4mm
Sampling Plan: 5-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Surfscan SP5 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Optical Overlay Metrology' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Micro-cracks defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 3nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 99 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 96% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±1.4% for Optical Overlay Metrology
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.96 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-04-04
Wafers Tested: 45
Total Defects Found: 2689
Defect Density: 380.42 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 7.6%
Capture Rate: 92.2%
Test Duration: 377 minutes
System Uptime: 97.6%

Result Classification: PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Surfscan SP5 demonstrated excellent performance in detecting Micro-cracks at the 3nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Cross-correlation with the reference SEM confirmed classification accuracy.

e) The defect review station correlation was within specification.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS: No corrective actions required. Test passed all acceptance criteria.
